text:
Alex Chen: Quick sync — proposing SDK connector resilience + pagination defaults. TL;DR: central `connectors` policy that owns retry/backoff, pagination semantics, and idempotency keys. Thin per-language adapters translate ergonomics. RFC draft linked: https://redwood.ai/rfc/connector-resilience. Thoughts?

Mira Patel: I like centralizing defaults, but worried about Go ergonomics. Go users expect explicit cursors and minimal allocations. Can we keep adapter surface thin for Go?

Jon L: Strong +1 to not leaking transport internals. SDKs should provide a consistent iterator/stream abstraction so apps don't need to switch logic when we fallback from streaming -> paged.

Kevin G: Two practical concerns: (1) idempotency markers for operations that may be retried, (2) resume token stability across model/infra rollouts. We should version resume tokens or include a stable envelope.

Alex Chen: Example of proposed policy shape (pseudo-config):
```
connectors.DefaultPolicy = {
  retry: { maxAttempts: 5, backoff: 'exponential', baseMs: 100 },
  pagination: { mode: 'cursor', pageSize: 100, resumeTokenKey: 'next_cursor' },
  idempotency: { header: 'Idempotency-Key' }
}
```
Adapters translate this into language-idiomatic helpers.

Mira Patel: For Python/TS we can hide cursor vs page by returning an async iterator with `resume()` support. For Go, return a `Cursor` type with explicit `Next(ctx)` to avoid heap churn.

Jon L: Important: SDK must preserve retry/dedup guarantees when switching transport at runtime. If we fallback from streaming to paged, iterator should be able to resume transparently or surface a clear error. We should document exactly what guarantees we provide (at-most-once vs at-least-once).

Kevin G: Agree. Also clarify prefetch semantics: if we allow parallel prefetch we need to warn that ordering/duplicates may occur. Default should be sequential prefetch to be safe.

Mira Patel: Suggest exposing a small `PolicyBuilder` API for power users so they can tweak `maxAttempts`, `maxInFlightPages`, and `resumeTolerance`. Keep it hidden for beginners.

Alex Chen: Operational hooks we need: telemetry events per retry reason, histogram of retry counts, and a policy-id tag so the Console can map metrics back to policy. Also consider a runtime flag to force paged-only for debugging.

ci-bot: RFC draft updated at https://redwood.ai/rfc/connector-resilience (v0.3)

Jon L: Action items: (1) Alex to land adapter contract in RFC, (2) Mira to prototype py/ts iterator shape, (3) Kevin to add resume-token compatibility tests and idempotency cases.

Alex Chen: Sounds good. I'll update RFC today and schedule a quick sync Thu 10:00am. :thumbsup:

Mira Patel: I'll start a small prototype branch and ping here when ready.

Kevin G: I'll sketch tests and include a failing test to lock shape.

Jon L: Thanks all — keeping this lightweight but important.
